access: Phishing, viruses and other attacks against users to obtain many user API keys, 2FA codes and other data
detection: The withdrawal triggered internal alarms after it executed; withdrawals stopped immediately afterwards
response: Deposits and withdrawals suspended for about a week; loss covered by the SAFU fund
ibs_note: Withdrawals were requested through genuine but stolen user credentials, so the exchange's own system signed them. IBS binds signatures to user-authenticated intents, which does not help when the user's own authentication is stolen; an exposure budget (C3) on a single 7,000 BTC transaction and pre-execution anomaly checks are the relevant controls. Partial coverage.

victim: Ronin Network bridge (Sky Mavis / Axie Infinity)
access: Penetration of Sky Mavis IT infrastructure (social engineering reported); a stale Axie DAO allowlist arrangement let the attacker obtain the fifth validator signature via a gas-free RPC node
detection: Six days later (March 29), after a user could not withdraw 5,000 ETH; no monitoring had detected the drain
response: Bridge and Katana DEX halted; validator set enlarged; FBI attribution to Lazarus Group
ibs_note: Withdrawals were signed by compromised validator keys, so a signer-side check bound to source-chain deposit evidence (the bridge's equivalent of an intent, C1) is the relevant control, and the six-day detection gap is the clearest case for an independent reconciling watcher (C4). IBS does not prevent theft of the keys themselves.

access: Compromise of multisig signer keys, likely via social engineering of team members (Elliptic)
detection: Same day; Harmony announced the theft June 23-24
response: FBI attribution to Lazarus Group and APT38 (Jan 23, 2023); part of the funds frozen
ibs_note: Two stolen keys sufficed under a low multisig threshold. IBS cannot stop theft of signing keys; per-withdrawal intent binding to deposit evidence (C1, if enforced on-chain or by every signer), exposure budgets (C3) and a watcher (C4) limit and detect the drain.
disputed: Multisig threshold reported as 2-of-5 (Mudit Gupta via The Block) and 2-of-4 (PeckShield via The Record)

access: Social engineering of an employee at Ginco (DMM's wallet-software provider) via a fake LinkedIn recruiter and a malicious "pre-employment test" script (March 2024); stolen session cookies used to impersonate the employee (mid-May)
detection: Unauthorized outflow detected by DMM Bitcoin on May 31, 2024
response: FBI/DC3/Japan NPA attribution (TraderTraitor) on Dec 23-24, 2024; DMM Bitcoin agreed to transfer accounts and assets to SBI VC Trade (Dec 2, 2024)
ibs_note: Law enforcement states the attackers manipulated a legitimate transaction request from a DMM employee, which is the signing-request manipulation class IBS targets; binding the signature to an independently issued intent (C1) and a per-transaction exposure limit (C3) apply directly.
disputed: Loss given as $305M or $308M depending on valuation time

access: Disputed: WazirX attributes it to a discrepancy in the custody provider Liminal's interface; Liminal attributes it to three compromised WazirX devices
response: Withdrawals halted; police report, FIU and CERT-In notified; WazirX ended its relationship with Liminal (Aug 14)
ibs_note: Signers approved a transaction whose displayed details differed from its contents (both parties agree on the mismatch, not on its origin). An independent intent check on the actual payload and default denial of contract upgrades would apply in either version.
disputed: Root cause (Liminal UI vs WazirX devices) is disputed between the two firms; the Grant Thornton review commissioned by Liminal found no compromise of Liminal's web application

access: Malware delivered via Telegram (impersonated former contractor, Sep 11) compromised at least three developers' devices
detection: Security monitoring alerts fired (ownership transfer, contract upgrade) during the attack
response: Lending markets paused; Mandiant engaged; signer set reduced to 7 with a 4-of-7 threshold
ibs_note: Hardware wallets blind-signed payloads replaced by malware while the interface showed legitimate data; ownership transfer of the lending pool provider is exactly the operation a deny-by-default policy (C2) would refuse without a dedicated, independently issued intent; alerts existed, so autonomous containment (C4) is the comparison point.
disputed: Loss reported as about $50M (post-mortem) to $53M (including approvals drained)

access: Supply chain: a Safe{Wallet} developer workstation was compromised (Feb 4, via a malicious Docker project per Safe); attacker used its AWS access to inject JavaScript into the Safe{Wallet} front end served from S3
detection: Bybit detected unauthorized activity during the routine cold-to-hot transfer, same day
response: FBI attribution (TraderTraitor/Lazarus) on Feb 26; malicious JavaScript removed by the attacker minutes after the theft
ibs_note: Signers approved what the tampered interface showed. IBS would require the signed payload to match an independently issued intent (the planned transfer to Bybit's hot wallet) and deny the delegatecall/implementation change by default; this holds only if the IBS check runs outside the compromised interface and signer workstations.
disputed: Loss figures range $1.4B-$1.5B by source and valuation time

access: Unauthorized access to a privileged management address (key compromise likely; how it was obtained is not public)
detection: Same day; Cyvers flagged the transactions; UPCX suspended deposits and withdrawals
response: Operations suspended; stolen tokens initially remained at the recipient address
ibs_note: A stolen admin key upgraded the ProxyAdmin and called withdrawByAdmin on three management accounts. IBS cannot stop a stolen key used directly on-chain; on-chain policy (timelocked upgrades, C2), withdrawal limits (C3) and upgrade monitoring with automatic pause (C4) limit it.
attacker_model: none (direct key use; on-chain policy not yet modelled)

access: Compromise of the project multisig (private key leak reported); attacker executed delegateCall, removed the admin role and added itself as owner
detection: Same day; Cyvers and on-chain observers flagged it
response: Exchanges froze much of the stolen assets; token migration to a new fixed-supply contract
ibs_note: Multisig control was seized and used to drain stablecoins and mint tokens. Default denial of delegateCall/owner changes (C2) and outflow limits with automatic containment (C3, C4) apply; how signing authority was obtained is not public, so C1's relevance is unknown.
disputed: Loss $11.3M (Cyvers) vs more than $30M (Hacken) vs about $41M including minted-token sales (Rekt)

access: Months-long social engineering of contributors, including in-person contact at crypto conferences (Drift); attackers prepared durable-nonce transactions from March 23
detection: Same day; the drain completed within about 12-20 minutes of the admin takeover
response: Deposits and withdrawals suspended; Drift attributes the attack (medium-high confidence) to UNC4736 (AppleJeus/Citrine Sleet); Elliptic and TRM report DPRK indicators
ibs_note: Security Council members signed admin-transfer transactions weeks earlier believing them harmless; Solana durable nonces kept those signatures valid indefinitely. Intent binding with an expiry and a declared purpose (C1), default denial of admin transfer and withdrawal-limit removal (C2), and exposure limits (C3) apply; IBS would have to run at each council signer, outside the attacker-influenced workflow.
disputed: Loss $280M (Drift) to $285-286M (PeckShield, Elliptic); dataset lists $295M. Dataset technique "Proxy Upgrade Hijack" understates the signing-path cause

chains: Ethereum, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Tron, Zcash and others
access: Breach of a critical backend system within the exchange's wallet infrastructure (CEO statement)
detection: Bitget's security systems detected unauthorized transfers at 18:31 UTC, Sept 24, 2026
response: Withdrawals suspended and resumed in phases from Sept 28; loss covered by the User Protection Fund (over $464M); CEO attributes the attack to North Korea based on on-chain analysis and IP patterns
ibs_note: Per the CEO, attackers spoofed transaction data and triggered Bitget's own authorization and signing process, which is the signing-request manipulation class IBS targets; intent binding (C1) and exposure budgets on hot/warm tiers (C3) apply directly. Root-cause report details beyond the CEO statement not yet reviewed.
disputed: Loss revised from $351.6M to $387.5M after tracing Zcash and Tron assets; attribution is the company's, not law enforcement's

chains: Ethereum and about nine other chains (10 total), including XRP, Arbitrum
access: Attacker reached a service container in Binance's withdrawal/signing infrastructure (reported); attacker infrastructure funded via Tornado Cash on Oct 28
detection: Same evening; hot wallet emptied 20:20-20:24 UTC; deposits and withdrawals paused
response: Stablecoin issuers froze funds (Tether about 971M USDT, Circle about 823M USDC); Arbitrum Security Council moved about $30M; Binance reports about $3B frozen and states it found no evidence of private key leak and will cover losses
ibs_note: The reference incident for this research: the exchange's own signer signed EIP-7702 delegations and withdrawals requested by compromised orchestration. Reproduced in the testbed (A1); IBS configurations R2-R4 contained it in simulation and on Besu (see testbed/results).
disputed: Total loss estimates $6.3B (Binance) and $6.36B (TRM Labs, via Wikipedia); attribution to TraderTraitor reported but not confirmed by law enforcement as of 2026-10-31
